item.title: Los fondos de inversión ganan terreno en Ecuador en este 2026; conozca cómo funcionan
item.author: Lucía Vásconez
item.description:
Los fondos de inversión ganan terreno en Ecuador en este 2026; conozca cómo funcionan
2026-08-30
Por Lucía Vásconez
https://www.primicias.ec/economia/fondos-inversion-ecuador-ahorros-funcionan-consejos-invertir-131350/
Los fondos de inversión ganan terreno en Ecuador en este 2026; conozca cómo funcionan
Los fondos de inversión en Ecuador administran USD 3.115 millones. Conozca cómo funcionan, dónde invierten, sus riesgos y cuánto dinero se necesita para empezar.
Un fondo de inversión reúne el dinero de varias personas o empresas para invertirlo conjuntamente en distintos activos y mercados.
- Foto
Pexels
Autor:
Actualizada:
Compartir:
Los fondos de inversión administran USD 3.115 millones en Ecuador, en un mercado que ha ganado espacio dentro del sistema financiero del país.
A agosto de 2026, existen 85 fondos activos, según el Catastro Público del Mercado de Valores de la Superintendencia de Compañías, Valores y Seguros (SCVS).
El primer fondo de inversión de Ecuador nació en 1992, pero el mayor crecimiento del sector se concentra en la última década. En siete años, el patrimonio administrado aumentó 411%, al pasar de USD 609 millones en 2019 a USD 3.115 millones en julio de 2026, señaló Gregorio Moreno, director de Negocios de Fondos de Inversión en Fideval.
Este crecimiento lo atribuye a la transformación del sector financiero, al acceso a la tecnología y a una mayor búsqueda de alternativas de ahorro.
¿Qué es un fondo de inversión?
Un fondo de inversión es un instrumento financiero de inversión colectiva. Varias personas aportan dinero para invertirlo en distintos activos y buscar un rendimiento o ganancias.
Una empresa especializada, que puede ser una Administradora de Fondos y Fideicomisos o fiduciaria, se encarga de gestionar esos recursos. Los 85 fondos activos están administrados por 34 de estas empresas.
Su objetivo es generar ganancias y diversificar las inversiones para reducir los riesgos, explicó Diego Peña, asesor de inversiones y docente de la Universidad Andina Simón Bolívar.
Cada fondo tiene un reglamento que establece en qué puede invertir y qué operaciones puede realizar. Además, el fondo es independiente de la empresa que lo administra.
Los rendimientos que genera el fondo, una vez descontados los gastos administrativos, se distribuyen entre los participantes de acuerdo con el monto que cada uno aportó.
¿Dónde se invierte el dinero?
Los fondos pueden invertir en productos bancarios y en instrumentos del mercado de valores. Entre ellos están los depósitos a plazo fijo y depósitos a la vista, agregó Peña.
También pueden colocar recursos en deuda de empresas privadas, obligaciones de largo plazo, papel comercial y pagarés, en el mercado de valores. El tipo de inversión depende del reglamento de cada fondo.
¿Con cuánto dinero se puede empezar?
Una de las principales características de estos fondos es que permiten realizar aportes periódicos.
Peña señala que en Ecuador existen opciones en las que una persona puede empezar con USD 25 al mes. El inversionista establece un aporte mínimo y luego puede mantenerlo o aumentarlo.
Esto marca una diferencia frente a alternativas como los depósitos a plazo fijo, que requieren colocar una cantidad de dinero alta de una sola vez y mantenerla durante un plazo determinado.
Invertir en varios activos para reducir el riesgo
El dinero de los participantes permite al fondo comprar diferentes activos. Esta estrategia se conoce como diversificación.
En lugar de concentrar todo el dinero en una empresa, por ejemplo, el fondo puede invertir en varias. Así, si una inversión tiene problemas de pago, las demás pueden continuar generando rendimientos. Esto puede reducir el riesgo de pérdida, aunque ninguna inversión está libre de riesgo.
¿Qué ventajas tienen?
Además de permitir aportes pequeños y periódicos, los fondos ofrecen administración profesional. Las fiduciarias toman las decisiones de inversión de acuerdo con las reglas establecidas para cada fon
[Transcripcion recortada]

item.title: Hombre murió tras recibir dos disparos durante un robo en Tumbaco; acudía a realizar un pago de pensiones
item.author: Redacción Primicias
item.description:
Hombre murió tras recibir dos disparos durante un robo en Tumbaco; acudía a realizar un pago de pensiones
2026-08-29
Por Redacción Primicias
https://www.primicias.ec/sucesos/balacera-villa-vega-herido-tumbaco-quito-cierre-vias-policia-131307/
Hombre murió tras recibir dos disparos durante un robo en Tumbaco; acudía a realizar un pago de pensiones
Un hombre de 33 años murió tras ser herido durante un asalto registrado en el sector de Villavega, en el nororiente de Quito. La víctima fue trasladada de urgencia a un hospital, pero, pese a las labores de reanimación, no fue posible salvarle la vida.
Personal de la Policía Nacional en el sector de Villavega, en Tumbaco, tras la balacera registrada el 28 de agosto de 2026.
- Foto
Policía Nacional
Autor:
Actualizada:
Compartir:
A las 10:22 del 28 de agosto de 2026 se registró una nueva balacera en Ecuador, esta vez en el sector de la Villavega en la parroquia de Tumbaco, nororiente de Quito.
El jefe de operaciones de Tumbaco, Byron Moreno, informó a PRIMICIAS que un ciudadano se acercó a una entidad a realizar un pago de pensiones alimenticias cuando fue víctima de asalto y robo.
Debido al forcejeo, se registraron detonaciones por arma de fuego y dos de los disparos impactaron en la mano y abdomen de la víctima de 33 años, según la Policía Nacional.
El ciudadano recibió primeros auxilios por parte del Cuerpo de Bomberos de Quito. Además, la Policía resaltó que, tras coordinar con el Ministerio de Salud, la víctima fue trasladada al hospital de Calderón, donde se confirmó su muerte.
De acuerdo con el Cuerpo de Bomberos de Quito, la víctima sufrió al menos tres paros cardiorrespiratorios en el hospital. Pese a las labores de reanimación, no fue posible salvarle la vida.
La AMT informó que se realizó un cierre vial en la avenida Oswaldo Guayasamín en el carril izquierdo en el sentido Valle-Quito.
A las 12:20 del viernes, personal de Criminalística llegó al sector para recabar indicios y realizar los trabajos correspondientes, debido a la presencia de balas en la calle.
Muertes violentas en Ecuador
Entre enero y julio de 2026, el país acumuló un total de 4.882 homicidios intencionales, lo que marca una reducción frente a los 5.295 casos reportados en el mismo lapso de 2025.
Esta aparente mejora nacional esconde un repunte reciente de violencia criminal. Durante los meses de junio y julio de 2026, las muertes violentas superaron a las del mismo periodo de 2025, rompiendo la tendencia a la baja observada al inicio del año y superando al que hasta ahora es el peor año de la historia.
Al analizar la serie histórica, se evidencia otro dato. Las cifras de junio con 693 muertes y julio con 704 casos en 2026 se mantuvieron por debajo de las de 2023, que se posicionaba como el segundo año más violento de la historia.
Compartir:

A las 10:22 del 28 de agosto de 2026 se registró una nueva balacera en Ecuador, esta vez en el sector de la Villavega en la parroquia de Tumbaco, nororiente de Quito.
El jefe de operaciones de Tumbaco, Byron Moreno, informó a PRIMICIAS que un ciudadano se acercó a una entidad a realizar un pago de pensiones alimenticias cuando fue víctima de asalto y robo.
Debido al forcejeo, se registraron detonaciones por arma de fuego y dos de los disparos impactaron en la mano y abdomen de la víctima de 33 años, según la Policía Nacional.
El ciudadano recibió primeros auxilios por parte del Cuerpo de Bomberos de Quito. Además, la Policía resaltó que, tras coordinar con el Ministerio de Salud, la víctima fue trasladada al hospital de Calderón, donde se confirmó su muerte.
De acuerdo con el Cuerpo de Bomberos de Quito, la víctima sufrió al menos tres paros cardiorrespiratorios en el hospital. Pese a las labores de reanimación, no fue posible salvarle la vida.
La AMT informó que se realizó un cierre vial en la avenida Oswaldo Guayasamín en el carril izquierdo en el sentido Valle-Quito.
A las 12:20 del viernes, personal de Criminalística llegó al sector para recabar indicios y realizar los trabajos correspondientes, debido a la presencia de balas en la calle.
Muertes violentas en Ecuador
Entre enero y julio de 2026, el país acumuló un total de 4.882 homicidios intencionales, lo que marca una reducción frente a los 5.295 casos reportados en el mismo lapso de 2025.
Esta aparente mejora nacional esconde un repunte reciente de violencia criminal. Durante los meses de junio y julio de 2026, las muertes violentas superaron a las del mismo periodo de 2025, rompiendo la tendencia a la baja observada al inicio del año y superando al que hasta ahora es el peor año de la historia.
Al analizar la serie histórica, se evidencia otro dato. Las cifras de junio con 693 muertes y julio con 704 casos en 2026 se mantuvieron por debajo de las de 2023, que se posicionaba como el segundo año más violento de la historia.
Compartir:

item.title: Expresidente Lenín Moreno es condenado a cinco años de cárcel por el caso Sinohydro
item.author: Mario Alexis González
item.description:
Expresidente Lenín Moreno es condenado a cinco años de cárcel por el caso Sinohydro
2026-08-29
Por Mario Alexis González
https://www.primicias.ec/politica/vivo-lectura-sentencia-lenin-moreno-caso-sinohydro-131276/
Expresidente Lenín Moreno es condenado a cinco años de cárcel por el caso Sinohydro
Lenín Moreno fue condenado a cinco años de prisión por cohecho en el caso Sinohydro y no podrá volver a ejercer cargos públicos. También fue condenado su entorno familiar, el lobista Conto Patiño, un exembajador y exejecutivos de la empresa china.
El expresidente Lenín Moreno y su esposa Rocío González ingresan a recibir la sentencia por el caso Sinohydro, el 28 de agosto de 2026, en la Corte Nacional de Justicia.
- Foto
API
Autor:
Actualizada:
Compartir:
Un Tribunal de la Corte Nacional de Justicia (CNJ) reinstaló este 28 de agosto de 2026 la audiencia de juicio del caso Sinohydro para emitir su veredicto. El proceso investiga un presunto cohecho ligado a la central hidroeléctrica Coca Codo Sinclair.
La Fiscalía sostiene que la constructora china Sinohydro habría pagado USD 76,1 millones en coimas para adjudicarse la obra y su crédito. El principal acusado como autor directo es el expresidente y exvicepresidente de la República, Lenín Moreno.
La acusación señala como cómplices al círculo de Moreno: su esposa, Rocío González; su hija Irina Moreno; sus hermanos Edwin y Guillermo Moreno; y su cuñada Martha González, por supuestos fondos recibidos mediante firmas offshore.
En la trama figura como autor directo el lobista Conto Patiño, junto a sus hijos María Auxiliadora, Juan Carlos, Patricia y Manuel Patiño, y su yerno Xavier Macías, señalados por supuestamente canalizar y distribuir los dineros ilícitos.
La sentencia
La sentencia de primera instancia fue dictada por parte del Tribunal integrado por los jueces Manuel Cabrera Esquivel (ponente), Daniella Camacho y Julio Inga Yanza. La resolución todavía puede ser apelada.
- 28/08/2026 20:34 Cai Runguo, exembajador de China en Ecuador y dos ejecutivos de Sinohydro son condenados a cinco años de cárcelPor unanimidad, el tribunal también condenó a cinco años de cárcel a Cai Rungo, exembajador de China en Ecuador, y a dos ejecutivos de Sinohydro, en calidad de autores directos de cohecho.
- 28/08/2026 20:23 Tribunal condena a cinco años de cárcel a Lenín Moreno y al lobista Conto PatiñoCon una pena de cinco años de cárcel, y la "incapacidad perpetua para el desempeño de ejercer cargo público", fue condenado el expresidente Lenín Moreno, en calidad de autor de cohecho en el caso Sinohydro. En tanto que Rocío González, esposa del exmandatario, y su hija Irene Moreno, así como sus hermanos Guillermo y Edwin Moreno fueron condenados a dos años y seis meses, en calidad de cómplices, al igual que el abogado Eduardo Cargminiani. El lobista Conto Patiño también deberá pugar cinco años de cárcel. Mientras que cuatro de sus hijos (María Auxiliadora, Patricia, Manuel Ignacio y Juan Carlos), y su yerno Xavier Macías, fueron condenados a dos años y seis meses de prisión.
- 28/08/2026 20:11 Tribunal ordena a Lenín Moreno devolver el triple de los beneficios recibidos por cohechoEl tribunal determinó que, en todos los casos de cohecho analizados, la restitución económica corresponde al triple del monto del que se habría beneficiado cada procesado, de acuerdo con la sentencia. Así, las personas declaradas autoras o cómplices deberán restituir tres veces el beneficio económico individualmente atribuido, incluidos los familiares y allegados de Lenín Moreno y los procesados vinculados al esquema de Sinohydro
- 28/08/2026 20:08 Exembajador de China declarado culpable de cohechoEn el caso Sinohydro están involucradas una veintena de personas, entre ellos varios chinos como Cai Runguo, exembajador en Quito, quien fue declarado autor directo de cohecho.
- 28/08/2026 18:58 Abogados Eduardo Carmigniani y Carlos Almeida, declarados cómplices de cohechoOtro procesado José Eduardo Carminiani Valen
[Transcripcion recortada]

item.title: Trump anuncia un acuerdo con Venezuela para controlar 65.000 millones de barriles de las reservas petroleras del país | CNN
item.author: Kit Maher
item.description:
Trump anuncia un acuerdo con Venezuela para controlar 65.000 millones de barriles de las reservas petroleras del país | CNN
2026-08-29
Por Kit Maher
https://cnnespanol.cnn.com/2026/08/28/latinoamerica/trump-acuerdo-venezuela-barriles-petroleo-trax
El presidente Donald Trump dijo el viernes por la noche que Estados Unidos llegó a un acuerdo petrolero con Venezuela, una medida que, según afirmó, más que duplicará las reservas petroleras estadounidenses, aumentará el suministro de petróleo y reducirá los precios de la gasolina.
“Bajo mis instrucciones, el secretario de Estado, Marco Rubio, y el secretario de Guerra, Pete Hegseth, trabajando estrechamente con la muy respetada presidenta interina de Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez, y mediante una alianza con empresas privadas, han asegurado el control mayoritario de Estados Unidos sobre más de 65.000 MILLONES DE BARRILES de reservas probadas de petróleo en Venezuela, sin costo alguno para el contribuyente estadounidense”, dijo Trump en redes sociales.
El énfasis de Trump en reducir los precios de la gasolina, a casi dos meses de las elecciones intermedias de Estados Unidos, se produce cuando el precio promedio nacional supera los US$ 1,06 por litro.
La guerra con Irán ha interrumpido durante seis meses una quinta parte del suministro mundial de petróleo, pero en las últimas semanas llegó a un punto de inflexión: miles de millones de barriles de petróleo y combustible almacenados en reservas comerciales han desaparecido. Las reservas de emergencia de Estados Unidos no habían sido tan reducidas desde principios de la década de 1980, mientras los inversionistas del mercado de bonos y los votantes pierden la paciencia ante los altos precios.
“Esta transacción histórica MÁS QUE DUPLICA las reservas petroleras estadounidenses, aumenta considerablemente nuestro suministro de petróleo y reducirá sustancialmente los precios de la gasolina para todos los estadounidenses durante muchos años, al tiempo que ayuda a mantener a Venezuela en el camino hacia un éxito enorme y una gran prosperidad. ¡Esta transacción fortalecerá enormemente la relación, ya en expansión, entre Venezuela y Estados Unidos!”, escribió Trump en su publicación.
Rodríguez también destacó el acuerdo entre ambos países.
“Nuestro objetivo es avanzar hacia la consolidación de nuestra posición como potencia productora de energía, poniendo nuestras inmensas reservas al servicio del desarrollo nacional, la creación de empleo, el aumento de los ingresos de nuestros trabajadores y el bienestar de nuestro pueblo”, dijo en un comunicado el viernes por la noche.
Un funcionario de la Casa Blanca dijo a CNN que el acuerdo negociado otorgará a Estados Unidos “el control efectivo del 55 % de la producción de una nueva empresa conjunta privada, que será la segunda petrolera privada más grande del mundo por volumen de reservas”.
Con el apoyo de Estados Unidos, dijo el funcionario, Rodríguez otorgó a una empresa privada concesiones por 100 años para explotar los yacimientos petroleros. El funcionario añadió que la empresa es un proyecto conjunto del Gobierno de Estados Unidos y un operador privado en Venezuela.
“El Gobierno de Estados Unidos ha asegurado más de la mitad del valor de este nuevo gigante petrolero, dividido entre una participación accionaria y compromisos garantizados de compra a costo. A medida que la empresa amplíe la producción, el suministro estable de petróleo a costo que genere en nuestro hemisferio se destinará a reabastecer la Reserva Estratégica de Petróleo de Estados Unidos y a cubrir las necesidades de suministro de las Fuerzas Armadas de Estados Unidos”, dijo el funcionario.
Rubio calificó el acuerdo como “una enorme victoria tanto para el pueblo estadounidense como para el venezolano”.
“Para el pueblo venezolano, este acuerdo generará cerca de US$ 100.000 millones en inversión privada, respaldará miles de empleos bien remunerados e impulsará la reconstrucción de la economía de Venezuela”, dijo Rubio poco d
[Transcripcion recortada]

“Nuestro objetivo es avanzar hacia la consolidación de nuestra posición como potencia productora de energía, poniendo nuestras inmensas reservas al servicio del desarrollo nacional, la creación de empleo, el aumento de los ingresos de nuestros trabajadores y el bienestar de nuestro pueblo”, dijo en un comunicado el viernes por la noche.
Un funcionario de la Casa Blanca dijo a CNN que el acuerdo negociado otorgará a Estados Unidos “el control efectivo del 55 % de la producción de una nueva empresa conjunta privada, que será la segunda petrolera privada más grande del mundo por volumen de reservas”.
Con el apoyo de Estados Unidos, dijo el funcionario, Rodríguez otorgó a una empresa privada concesiones por 100 años para explotar los yacimientos petroleros. El funcionario añadió que la empresa es un proyecto conjunto del Gobierno de Estados Unidos y un operador privado en Venezuela.
“El Gobierno de Estados Unidos ha asegurado más de la mitad del valor de este nuevo gigante petrolero, dividido entre una participación accionaria y compromisos garantizados de compra a costo. A medida que la empresa amplíe la producción, el suministro estable de petróleo a costo que genere en nuestro hemisferio se destinará a reabastecer la Reserva Estratégica de Petróleo de Estados Unidos y a cubrir las necesidades de suministro de las Fuerzas Armadas de Estados Unidos”, dijo el funcionario.
Rubio calificó el acuerdo como “una enorme victoria tanto para el pueblo estadounidense como para el venezolano”.
“Para el pueblo venezolano, este acuerdo generará cerca de US$ 100.000 millones en inversión privada, respaldará miles de empleos bien remunerados e impulsará la reconstrucción de la economía de Venezuela”, dijo Rubio poco d
[Transcripcion recortada]

item.title: Retailers feel the sting as cautious consumers weigh their options
item.author: Hamza Shaban
item.description:
Retailers feel the sting as cautious consumers weigh their options
2026-08-29
Por Hamza Shaban
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/retailers-feel-the-sting-as-cautious-consumers-weigh-their-options-100000047.html
The biggest theme this earnings season for retailers was trade-offs: between price and profit, promotions and growth, and getting customers through the door while household budgets are under pressure.
For the luckiest and best-executing companies, the value proposition drew consumers in.
With gas prices eating into wallets, the trade-down or value proposition of stores like Target (TGT) and Dollar General (DG) made an otherwise tough shopping choice easier to manage.
A twist this season was the impact of tariff refunds. Sure, fat checks from Uncle Sam padded corporate finances. But the refunds also brought in skepticism from investors and analysts. Did earnings beats and rosier outlooks stem from successful operations or the cash windfall that fell from the sky? (Or the Supreme Court, in this case.)
Even strong performances didn't automatically translate to wins on Wall Street. Walmart (WMT) and Dollar Tree (DLTR) highlighted that dynamic.
Dollar Tree beat analysts' expectations, but the stock fell 4% as the discount retailer's guidance for the current quarter disappointed. The chain was also a victim of sorts to the tariff refund: A healthy portion of its projected EPS for the current quarter comes from refund reinvestments. And even with that one-time exception, investors weren't pleased.
Walmart, for its part, posted US same-store sales that had the slowest pace of growth since the end of 2020, with traffic and ticket sizes coming in lower than expected. Whereas the executives of Lowe's (LOW) and Home Depot (HD) nodded to pressured and cautious consumers, Walmart's CFO pointed to the psychological impact of $4 gasoline and the trade-offs consumers are making.
One unambiguous bright spot in retail is the beauty category. From Walmart to Target, Estée Lauder (EL) to, most recently, Ulta (ULTA), which reported a beat and raised its outlook, at the end of the week, the growth of beauty merchandise reinforced the idea that the lipstick effect is in play. It might not be the right time to splurge on a bathroom renovation, golf clubs, or new clothes, but people are sticking to their skin care routine.
Other stores had stock stories defined by their individual quirks. Best Buy posted quarterly results on Thursday that surpassed Wall Street estimates as new technology boosted sales, but the stock fell 5% anyway. Shares had already risen more than 30% over the past six months, so it was tough to juice the ticker further without a blowout quarter. But the familiar and dominant theme cropped up: customers on the hunt for a bargain.

item.title: Warsh says AI could turbocharge the economy. The Fed is keeping close watch.
item.author: Jennifer Schonberger
item.description:
Warsh says AI could turbocharge the economy. The Fed is keeping close watch.
2026-08-29
Por Jennifer Schonberger
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/warsh-says-ai-could-turbocharge-the-economy-the-fed-is-keeping-close-watch-144209622.html
Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh suggested Friday that artificial intelligence could turbocharge the economy and that the central bank is closely monitoring its impact.
"The potential for substantially higher growth is on the rise. Ever-expanding pools of capital are pouring into AI-related infrastructure of all sorts," Warsh said in a closely watched speech in Jackson Hole, Wyo.
Warsh stressed that the Fed recognizes AI is potentially a new factor of production that will have consequences for both the economy and interest rates.
He said the central bank is watching the development of large language models at the heart of AI and the tokens used to access the models "attentively."
He also posed some key questions: whether the application of AI will spur a significant, sustained rise in productivity across the economy and, if so, when. Over time, then, how much of that value will accrue to businesses and consumers, and what are the broad implications for workers and the strength of the job market?
The Fed is considering these questions with a task force Warsh appointed earlier this year focused on productivity and jobs.
Warsh's comments come after he said in 2025 that he believed AI would significantly increase productivity and, as a result, push down inflation.

item.title: Warsh offered forward guidance after all, former Fed vice chair says
item.author: Jennifer Schonberger
item.description:
Warsh offered forward guidance after all, former Fed vice chair says
2026-08-29
Por Jennifer Schonberger
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/warsh-offered-forward-guidance-after-all-former-fed-vice-chair-says-190112766.html
Markets knew they weren't going to get an answer to what the Federal Reserve would do next — so-called forward guidance — when the central bank's chairman, Kevin Warsh, spoke on Friday morning. The biggest question looming over Warsh's highly anticipated speech was whether he would clarify how the Fed will respond to rising inflation.
On that, he delivered, former Fed vice chairman Alan Blinder, now a professor of economics at Princeton University, said in an interview with Yahoo Finance.
Warsh painted a robust picture of the US economy, noting that economic growth appears to have strengthened, while characterizing the labor market as stable at full employment. He underscored that inflation remains too high and that while this summer's inflation readings were better than expected, they "do not tell me that underlying trends have meaningfully improved."
"I would call that forward guidance," Blinder said. "He doesn't call it forward guidance … That sounded to me like somebody who thought interest rates should go up, right?"
Read more: Live updates and reaction to Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole speech
Blinder thinks a September rate hike is on the table, saying Warsh sounded "like a man who was rationalizing raising interest rates."
"My guess is they'll be raising rates in September, just a quarter of a point, and [then] they'll wait," he said.
Traders appear to agree. Odds of a September rate hike rose to nearly 60% following Warsh's speech, up from 35% on Thursday.
"Markets almost always want more clarity than policymakers can deliver," Blinder added. "There's a classic mismatch between the concreteness, I'll call it, that the markets are constantly craving. I think it's the case that Kevin Warsh wants to be a little less open than, say, [former Fed Chair] Jay Powell."
In his speech, Warsh laid out the data he's monitoring to set policy and reaffirmed that the Personal Consumption Expenditures index (PCE) is the Fed's preferred yardstick for inflation, after suggesting it may not be in July.
He said he is watching changes in the growth rates of corporate earnings and capital spending, as well as the follow-on effects on asset prices, business confidence, consumer incomes, and spending.
Another former Fed official weighs in
Esther George, former president of the Kansas City Federal Reserve, said she thought Warsh delivered a very good speech.
"Although he stopped short of saying 'and here's what we'll do about it,'" she said of his economic assessment, "I think it sets it up in a way that is true to what he set out to do, which is 'I'm not going to over promise, but I'm going to tell you what we're concerned about.'"

item.title: Fed Chairman Warsh says inflation is running too high, offers first assessment of economy
item.author: Jennifer Schonberger
item.description:
Fed Chairman Warsh says inflation is running too high, offers first assessment of economy
2026-08-28
Por Jennifer Schonberger
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/fed-chairman-warsh-says-inflation-is-running-too-high-offers-first-assessment-of-economy-140031752.html
Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh, in a closely watched speech Friday, said inflation is running too high and should be the focus for the central bank, while laying out a strong assessment of the economy for the first time. But he held to his pledge not to provide forward guidance.
"We must be confident that underlying inflation is moving to our objective, clearly and at sufficient speed. Otherwise, we have work to do," Warsh said in his first speech as chairman in Jackson Hole, Wyo. "It is the Fed's job to deliver stable prices."
While Warsh did not offer forward guidance, he hinted that interest rates may not be holding back the economy much, saying, "I would be hard-pressed to describe broad financial conditions as restrictive."
Warsh delivers the high-stakes speech as markets clamor for more clarity on whether the Fed has a credible strategy to bring down inflation and whether the chairman would offer an assessment of the economic picture. He came through on the latter; whether markets are satisfied on the strategy question will become clear in the reaction to the speech.
Pointing to the Personal Consumption Expenditures index, Warsh noted that "the numbers are more concerning."
He noted market measures of inflation expectations and stressed the importance of those signals reverberating back to the Fed.
"It is a credit to the Fed as an institution — and consistent with the best of the Fed's traditions — that market prices show confidence that we will deliver price stability. And I can assure you … they're right," he said.
Warsh noted that broad inflation measures have fallen significantly from their 2022 heights, but that progress over the past two years has been modest. He said that while this summer's PCE and Consumer Price Index readings were better than expected, "they do not tell me that underlying trends have meaningfully improved."
There have been questions about whether PCE would remain the central bank's preferred inflation gauge, given the doubt Warsh cast during his press conference in July. Warsh's mention of PCE on Friday seemed to suggest it will.
Soaring profits, stable labor market
Warsh painted a robust picture of the US economy, noting that economic growth appears to have strengthened, citing "rapidly rising" capital expenditures, which he estimates grew by 9% over the past four quarters.
Warsh noted that more than half of this year's capital expenditure growth is likely attributable to the artificial intelligence build-out. He noted that consumer spending adjusted for inflation has been healthy despite the surge in oil prices, tariffs, and other shocks, increasing by more than 2% over the past four quarters

item.title: Analysis-Bessent, Warsh diverge on who should set the price of money
item.author: Karen Brettell
item.description:
Analysis-Bessent, Warsh diverge on who should set the price of money
2026-08-28
Por Karen Brettell
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/analysis-bessent-warsh-diverge-set-050320832.html
By Karen Brettell
Aug 27 (Reuters) - Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh appear at odds over a question at the heart of U.S. financial policy. How hands-off can policymakers be when it comes to setting a price for money?
Warsh has advocated retreating from some of the central bank's longstanding communication policies in favor of letting markets do the heavy lifting, while Bessent has deployed a number of tools, some of them unusual, in the name of aiding market function.
The divide has come into view as the Trump administration steps up efforts to contain long-term borrowing costs — a push whose success appears unlikely to many analysts and portfolio managers without concrete steps to contain the sprawling U.S. fiscal deficit.
That contrast in approaches will come into focus on Friday morning, when Warsh is scheduled to speak at the Fed's annual event in Jackson Hole, Wyoming. He wants bond markets to play a bigger role in setting rates, a stance arguably at odds with Bessent's interventionism. Meanwhile investors are seeking assurance that Warsh will act decisively against inflation in his first year leading a divided Fed.
DOUBLING DOWN AT TREASURY
Bessent said last week Treasury would at least double buybacks of longer-dated debt, arguing that a rise in yields, which pushed 30-year rates to a 19-year high, didn't reflect fundamentals. Investors read it as a sign Washington won't let 10-year yields, which drive mortgage rates, approach 5% unanswered.
Many investors say Bessent is fighting the wrong fight. They say strong growth, sticky inflation, likely Fed hikes and heavy bond supply, including from AI-driven corporate borrowing, are what's pushing yields up, along with a widening fiscal premium tied to the deficit — not market dysfunction.
Billionaire investor Stanley Druckenmiller, a hedge-fund titan and workplace mentor to both men, called the plan "price management" rather than liquidity management and warned it could damage Treasury's credibility.
"There's very little evidence that Treasuries are oversold right now," said Will Compernolle, macro strategist at FHN Financial.
Traders say that pressure will surface elsewhere if bond yields aren't allowed to rise to a market-clearing price — including in a dollar that has slid since Bessent's announcement.
A SMALL BUYBACK, A LARGER SIGNAL
Bessent's strategy appears aimed at easing the economy's interest burden while preserving growth. He says Treasury has a large toolkit, but its influence over long-term yields is constrained by cash management, financing needs and that the U.S. will follow a predictable issuance schedule.

item.title: Oil settles up 2% after Trump rejects return to Iran ceasefire deal terms
item.author: Siddharth Cavale
item.description:
Oil settles up 2% after Trump rejects return to Iran ceasefire deal terms
2026-08-28
Por Siddharth Cavale
https://finance.yahoo.com/energy/articles/oil-extends-losses-on-hopes-middle-east-talks-could-ease-supply-woes-081929665.html
By Siddharth Cavale
NEW YORK, Aug 27 (Reuters) - Brent crude prices settled up by 2.1% on Thursday, snapping a three-session losing streak, after a Wall Street Journal report said U.S. President Donald Trump is not interested in returning to terms of a memorandum of understanding reached with Iran in June.
Citing people familiar with the matter, the report said the Trump administration has repeatedly told mediators it has no interest in reviving the June agreement, complicating a flurry of diplomatic efforts this week to restart talks.
Brent crude futures finished up $1.86, or 2.1% at $89.70 a barrel. U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude futures settled up $1.30, or 1.6% at $83.53.
Both benchmarks rebounded as investors scaled back expectations of a diplomatic breakthrough that could boost oil flows from the Middle East.
A lack of progress in talks, combined with continually restricted flows, could have prompted an adjustment of market views, UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo said.
Earlier on Thursday, Washington confirmed it was not in talks with Iran despite diplomatic efforts by other countries to re-engage the two sides.
"We don't want to speak to them. We're not looking to meet or anything," Trump told reporters later in the Oval Office, saying the U.S. was focused on punishing Tehran economically and would penalize countries that do business with the Islamic Republic.
On Monday, the U.S. announced what it called the "toughest sanctions in history" on Iran. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent suggested the measures would lessen the need for new major military operations.
Ebrahim Azizi, head of the Iranian parliament's national security committee, said the sanctions were an "inhumane and hostile act" that had nevertheless lost their effectiveness.
Qatar's prime minister visited Tehran on Thursday in a bid to relaunch diplomatic talks to end the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran, on the eve of its six-month anniversary.
Iran's top security official Mohsen Rezaei warned that Tehran would target U.S. military and economic interests if Washington started any "mischief" during the talks with Qatari officials.
PROLONGED UNCERTAINTY
"At the heart of the dispute remains Iran's nuclear programme and that is unlikely to be resolved quickly ... Iran also understands the importance of its geographical position and the leverage that the Strait of Hormuz provides, so the risk of prolonged uncertainty remains," said Priyanka Sachdeva, head of market insights at Phillip Nova.
The Strait of Hormuz handled about one-fifth of global daily oil and liquefied natural gas supplies before the conflict began in late February.

item.title: OpenAI, Anthropic Urge Cyber Defense Action as AI Models Improve
item.author: Rachel Metz
item.description:
OpenAI, Anthropic Urge Cyber Defense Action as AI Models Improve
2026-08-28
Por Rachel Metz
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/openai-anthropic-urge-cyber-defense-170920858.html
(Bloomberg) -- Artificial intelligence companies OpenAI and Anthropic PBC, along with more than 100 other tech and financial services organizations, warned that businesses and governments must do more to prepare for and defend against AI-enabled hacks.
Most Read from Bloomberg
In an open letter Thursday, the AI startups, along with Alphabet Inc.'s Google, Microsoft Corp. and others, called for organizations, governments and technology and AI companies to focus on making cyber defense "an immediate leadership priority" and to fix existing weaknesses in their own software.
The letter also asks cybersecurity companies to help defend against "AI-enabled attacks" and says governments should coordinate communication between themselves and industry channels to respond to potential threats. It also urges leading AI companies to give AI access, as well as financial support and training, to those that defend critical infrastructure.
The letter comes after several recent cybersecurity breaches involving advanced AI models, including an incident in July in which models from OpenAI inadvertently hacked Hugging Face Inc. The breaches have ignited concerns about AI agents running amok, and prompted some technology and government leaders to renew calls for curbs on the technology. On Wednesday, OpenAI said in a report that it could have reacted sooner to prevent the hack on Hugging Face.
The letter's signatories predicted that AI models will be used to carry out a growing number of increasingly complicated cyber attacks in the months ahead, as companies continue to build AI models that are capable at both defending against and carrying out such acts.
"Today's AI advances are already giving defenders new ways to fix weaknesses that have accumulated for years," the letter states. "If we act decisively, we can use the defenders' window to make our digital world much more secure."
Most Read from Bloomberg Businessweek
2026 Bloomberg L.P.

item.title: Kansas City Fed’s Schmid warns payment innovation will be ‘very disruptive’ Kansas City’s Schmid warns of disruption with the onset of new payment forms
item.author: Jennifer Schonberger
item.description:
Kansas City Fed’s Schmid warns payment innovation will be ‘very disruptive’ Kansas City’s Schmid warns of disruption with the onset of new payment forms
2026-08-28
Por Jennifer Schonberger
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/crypto/article/kansas-city-feds-schmid-warns-payment-innovation-will-be-very-disruptive-160834131.html
As central bankers gather for the 49th annual economic symposium in Jackson Hole, Wyo., starting Thursday evening, Kansas City Fed president Jeff Schmid warned that the rise of innovation in payments from stablecoins to blockchain and instantaneous payments could be disruptive.
"I think we're going to find that not only is this, from an innovation standpoint, very transitional, it's going to be very disruptive too," Schmid said in an interview with Yahoo Finance.
The theme of this year's gathering focuses on financial innovation in payments and the implications for monetary policy.
"I think we need to prepare," Schmid said. "We're going to be talking in the next decade more about sources of liquidity and duration, maybe more than we talked about capital, because at the end of the day, that $5 [trillion] or $10 trillion that we move a day is going to over time become instantaneous, and that's going to be a change in the system at large."
If payments become instantaneous and settle instantaneously, Schmid wonders, how does that impact liquidity, and what's the nature of assets backing the instruments?
One of those innovations — stablecoins — is mandated by a newly passed law to back all outstanding payment stablecoins on a strict 1-to-1 ratio with highly liquid, safe assets. Those assets include short-term US Treasurys, physical cash, or deposits.
Since stablecoins are mandated to be backed by short-term liquid assets, including T-bills, as the market grows, that could increase demand for stablecoin issuers holding Treasurys.
Read more: How stablecoins work
Schmid said that could have implications for financial stability. That's where the Fed comes in.
"What do we have to do relative to supervisory regulation just around how liquid a bank is?" said Schmid. "We've got architecture like that now, but you think about things like the Silicon Valley Bank experience and how fast that went from a capital impairment to a liquidity crisis, and that's the challenge instant payments are going to create.
"So from a financial stability standpoint, we need to be aware of these things."
Silicon Valley Bank failed in March 2023 after failing to hedge interest rate risk. It was deeply intertwined with the cryptocurrency sector and triggered a severe stablecoin run.
"So that's why I think not only is it financial innovation, it's an awareness that, hey, be prepared, because we've unleashed the instant payment platform and it's going to mature over the next decade."

item.title: Nvidia posted a blowout quarter. China remains a quagmire.
item.author: Jake Conley
item.description:
Nvidia posted a blowout quarter. China remains a quagmire.
2026-08-28
Por Jake Conley
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/nvidia-posted-a-blowout-quarter-china-remains-a-quagmire-122920310.html
Nvidia (NVDA) painted a bullish picture for investors when it reported its earnings after the bell on Wednesday, raising its guidance for the third quarter and beating analyst estimates across the board on revenue, earnings per share, and a host of other metrics.
Missing from that forward guidance, however, were sales projections into the world's second-largest economy — China, where Nvidia's ability to sell its chips has been snarled by state politics and national security concerns.
"Given ongoing geopolitical uncertainty, there is no China data center compute revenue in our forward outlook," Nvidia finance chief Collette Kress said during the company's earnings call on Wednesday.
That potential sales to Chinese buyers were left out of forward guidance from Nvidia gets at how complex the picture has become for one of the world's most valuable companies in its dealings with the US's largest AI competitor.
Nvidia said in its earnings report that it had stepped back into the Chinese market, if in a small way, with the first sales of its H200 chips, the leading semiconductor design from the company's "Hopper" line, a step down from its state-of-the-art Grace Blackwell chips. Yet those sales accounted for less than 1% of the $89 billion Nvidia recorded in data center revenue in the second quarter.
For Jensen Huang's company, complications come from both sides of the US-China AI arms race. Since 2022, Nvidia has wrestled with the Trump White House over sales of its chips to China, where even models such as the H200, which are now multiple generations behind Nvidia's flagship products, remain competitive with options available in China from companies like Huawei Technologies.
Huang won a key victory for his company after a concerted lobbying effort throughout 2025, securing permission for Nvidia to sell some H200 chips to Chinese buyers. But any optimism was quickly snarled by directives from Beijing to Chinese companies not to purchase the chips.
"Under the current rules and geopolitical landscape, we are unable to create and deliver a competitive product for wide distribution in China's data center market with the approval from both the USG and the Chinese government," Nvidia said Wednesday.
It's unclear exactly how many H200 chips were sold to Chinese buyers in the second quarter, but the count fell below the US limit due to blocks imposed by the Chinese government, Nvidia said. The company shouldered a $400 million charge related to "excess inventory" of H200 chips as demand has fallen off outside China, Nvidia said Wednesday.
item.content:encoded:
Nvidia posted a blowout quarter. China remains a quagmire.

2026-08-28

Por Jake Conley

https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/nvidia-posted-a-blowout-quarter-china-remains-a-quagmire-122920310.html

Nvidia (NVDA) painted a bullish picture for investors when it reported its earnings after the bell on Wednesday, raising its guidance for the third quarter and beating analyst estimates across the board on revenue, earnings per share, and a host of other metrics.

Missing from that forward guidance, however, were sales projections into the world's second-largest economy — China, where Nvidia's ability to sell its chips has been snarled by state politics and national security concerns.

"Given ongoing geopolitical uncertainty, there is no China data center compute revenue in our forward outlook," Nvidia finance chief Collette Kress said during the company's earnings call on Wednesday.

That potential sales to Chinese buyers were left out of forward guidance from Nvidia gets at how complex the picture has become for one of the world's most valuable companies in its dealings with the US's largest AI competitor.

Nvidia said in its earnings report that it had stepped back into the Chinese market, if in a small way, with the first sales of its H200 chips, the leading semiconductor design from the company's "Hopper" line, a step down from its state-of-the-art Grace Blackwell chips. Yet those sales accounted for less than 1% of the $89 billion Nvidia recorded in data center revenue in the second quarter.

For Jensen Huang's company, complications come from both sides of the US-China AI arms race. Since 2022, Nvidia has wrestled with the Trump White House over sales of its chips to China, where even models such as the H200, which are now multiple generations behind Nvidia's flagship products, remain competitive with options available in China from companies like Huawei Technologies.

Huang won a key victory for his company after a concerted lobbying effort throughout 2025, securing permission for Nvidia to sell some H200 chips to Chinese buyers. But any optimism was quickly snarled by directives from Beijing to Chinese companies not to purchase the chips.

"Under the current rules and geopolitical landscape, we are unable to create and deliver a competitive product for wide distribution in China's data center market with the approval from both the USG and the Chinese government," Nvidia said Wednesday.

It's unclear exactly how many H200 chips were sold to Chinese buyers in the second quarter, but the count fell below the US limit due to blocks imposed by the Chinese government, Nvidia said. The company shouldered a $400 million charge related to "excess inventory" of H200 chips as demand has fallen off outside China, Nvidia said Wednesday.

item.title: Dividends could be the next big Nvidia stock catalyst, just like they were for Apple
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Dividends could be the next big Nvidia stock catalyst, just like they were for Apple
2026-08-28
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/dividends-could-be-the-next-big-nvidia-stock-catalyst-just-like-they-were-for-apple-110850043.html
Nvidia (NVDA) being more generous with dividends and stock buybacks could be a nice catalyst for the stock, just as it has been for Apple (AAPL).
The AI chip darling returned a record $26 billion to shareholders in its second fiscal quarter, $20 billion through share repurchases and $6 billion by way of a $0.25 a share quarterly dividend. Relative to its plan to return 50% or more of free cash flow to shareholders, Nvidia has returned 60% year to date.
Executives said the company intends to increase capital returns going forward.
"We forecast Nvidia to return $115 billion in cash to shareholders in 2026 and $230b billion in 2027, which we expect will translate to P/E multiple expansion, similar to what happened to Apple in 2015," Evercore ISI analyst Mark Lipacis wrote in a note on Thursday.
Lipacis pointed out in the chart below that after five years of compression, Apple's price-to-earnings ratio began expanding with increases in its capital returns program.
Nvidia is certainly putting up the financial results to back up giving more cash back to shareholders.
Shares of Nvidia rose 6% on the company's second quarter results and upbeat outlook. Prior to the earnings report, Nvidia shares had slightly underperformed the S&P 500's year-to-date gain of about 14%.
Nvidia saw adjusted earnings per share of $2.22 on revenue of $96.2 billion. These were better than the $2.09 a share the Street had expected and revenue of $92.3 billion.
Nvidia's Data Center revenue, which includes Hyperscalers and AI Clouds, Industrial, and Enterprise (ACIE), came in at $89 billion versus a projected $85.8 billion.
Edge Computing, which includes Nvidia's other businesses, such as physical AI and gaming, brought in $7.2 billion. Analysts were expecting $6.6 billion.
Nvidia projected fiscal third quarter revenue of between $105.8 billion and $110.1 billion. Wall Street was calling for $105.1 billion.
This would be the first quarter above $100 billion in revenue for Nvidia, said Stifel analyst Ruben Roy.
Nvidia said it sees 70% revenue growth for fiscal year 2028. This was above analyst forecasts for 45% growth. The sales gain would be larger if not for memory chip shortages, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said.
"We see a clear path to $1 trillion revenue in fiscal year, supported by robust AI infrastructure demand and higher revenue per GW with Rubin. Despite gross margin reset to 72.5%, supply commitments increasing to $279 billion further strengthen our confidence in NVDA's visibility and ability to support the next phase of AI infrastructure deployments," Jefferies analyst Blayne Curtis said.

item.title: Dollar Tree stock falls despite earnings beat
item.author: Sam Boughedda
item.description:
Dollar Tree stock falls despite earnings beat
2026-08-28
Por Sam Boughedda
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/dollar-tree-stock-falls-despite-111212543.html
Investing.com -- Dollar Tree Inc. (NASDAQ:DLTR) reported second-quarter results that exceeded analyst expectations, but shares have dropped around 3% premarket as investors focused on weaker-than-expected third-quarter guidance.
The discount retailer posted adjusted earnings per share of $2.70, significantly surpassing the analyst consensus of $1.11. Revenue reached $4.9 billion, topping the estimate of $4.85 billion and representing a 7.0% increase YoY.
Comparable store net sales rose 3.7%, driven by a 3.3% increase in average ticket and a 0.4% increase in traffic. The quarter's results included a $1.31 per share benefit related to the net impact of tariff refunds.
However, the company's third quarter guidance disappointed investors. Dollar Tree expects adjusted EPS of $0.80 to $0.95, with a midpoint of $0.88 that includes an approximate $0.50 impact related to tariff refund reinvestments. It is below the consensus estimate of $1.39.
The company projects third-quarter comparable store net sales growth of 3.0% to 4.0% on revenue of $5.0 billion to $5.1 billion.
"What continues to set Dollar Tree apart is our ability to deliver value, convenience, and the excitement of discovery all in one shopping trip," said Mike Creedon, Chief Executive Officer. "Positive traffic trends helped drive strong comparable sales growth and EPS exceeded the high end of our outlook."
For the full fiscal year 2026, Dollar Tree raised its adjusted EPS outlook to a range of $7.70 to $8.05, with a midpoint of $7.88 that exceeds the analyst consensus of $7.04. This guidance includes an approximate $0.60 benefit related to the net impact of tariff refunds. The company expects full-year net sales of $20.5 billion to $20.7 billion based on comparable store net sales growth of 3% to 4%.

item.title: Nvidia says it's building an ecosystem that can't fail
item.author: Hamza Shaban
item.description:
Nvidia says it's building an ecosystem that can't fail
2026-08-28
Por Hamza Shaban
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/nvidia-says-its-building-an-ecosystem-that-cant-fail-153001892.html
Don't call it circular financing. Nvidia doesn't see its efforts to prop up upstarts and bolster key AI players as questionable financial engineering.
Yes, it's true that the beneficiaries of Nvidia's muscular backstops and investments are also its customers. But Nvidia doesn't see the scale of its support as something worthy of suspicion. That's because, the company says, it's building an ecosystem with too many scenarios for Nvidia to win.
A key question from critics of Nvidia concerns the demand for AI components, tools, and infrastructure: Would the growth around AI and the confident projections of future success be attainable without Nvidia's heavy hand?
CFO Colette Kress addressed the criticism head-on during the company's Q2 earnings call on Wednesday.
"We know some will call this circular financing. We see it differently. We are going through a major computing platform shift, the creation of one of the most important technologies in human history, and these are once-in-a-generation companies. Their technology leadership is proven, and their customer traction and usage are skyrocketing."
From Nvidia's perspective, the success of AI labs is independent of its partnerships. But why miss out on opportunities for more growth, greater revenue diversity, and the encouragement of other firms and would-be customers to put skin in the game?
And after all, Nvidia expects some of the frontier AI labs it's doing business with to become the largest tech companies in history (apologies to the Magnificent Seven).
But what's the difference between Nvidia's vision of a thriving AI ecosystem (with it at the financial and technological center) and a bullheaded belief that Nvidia is building a business environment that can't fail?
Nvidia has left some room for doubt. But not much.
"We believe these investments, measured against the strength of their demand, the business they create for us, the ecosystem they build on Nvidia's platform, and the equity returns on our invested capital will be excellent, and our risk is limited," Kress said on the call.
Demand from AI labs receiving some form of financial support from Nvidia will account for about a quarter of the company's business next year, Kress said.
A bullish reading on all of this is that Nvidia's true exposure to the debt they are helping finance for the AI build-out is narrow; that expanding its client base beyond the tech giants is a savvy bet-making; and that, in a rising-AI-tide that lifts all boats, Nvidia will be the one outfitting the vessels and helping to construct new ones.

item.title: As Jackson Hole conference kicks off, three Fed officials issue inflation warnings
item.author: Michael S Derby
item.description:
As Jackson Hole conference kicks off, three Fed officials issue inflation warnings
2026-08-28
Por Michael S Derby
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/jackson-hole-conference-kicks-off-143304791.html
As Jackson Hole conference kicks off, three Fed officials issue inflation warnings
By Michael S. Derby
5 min read
By Michael S. Derby
Aug 27 (Reuters) - Federal Reserve officials shared on Thursday their ongoing concerns about the U.S. inflation landscape, as central bankers gathered in Jackson Hole, Wyoming for the Kansas City Fed's closely watched annual economic symposium.
Inflation is "still stubborn and it's still sticky and we've got to continue to find ways to break through" and get it back to 2%, Kansas City Fed President Jeffrey Schmid said on CNBC on the sidelines of the conference.
He noted that the U.S. central bank's current policy rate, which was left in the 3.50%-3.75% range at the July 28-29 meeting, did not appear to be restrictive. "I don't know what we're restricting currently with the rate policy that we're at today," Schmid said.
Schmid, who had recently been in favor of raising rates to help bring inflation back down to the Fed's 2% target, seemed to suggest that he would still favor such a path, given his belief that monetary policy is not working to counter current price pressures.
But even so, when asked about the outlook for a rate hike at the Fed's September 15-16 policy meeting, he said, "I think we need a little bit more information. What I'm trying to figure out is the demand side of what's driving both growth and inflation."
Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, also speaking on CNBC, was similarly anxious about inflation and reiterated her ongoing willingness to act to bring price pressures back in line.
"I don't want to prejudge anything," Hammack said, "but I believe now is the time to act."
Hammack, one of three Fed officials who dissented at last month's meeting in favor of a rate hike, said inflation has been above target for more than five years and monetary policy is not doing anything at the moment to restrain the economy in order to lower price pressures.
The Cleveland Fed chief said she is hearing more and more from contacts worried about inflation and she fears the longer this trend continues, the greater the risk to the central bank's credibility. Information from local contacts suggests "we're starting to get some of that inflationary mindset" embedding itself in the economy. "I don't think we're there yet, but that's what I want to make sure we avoid," Hammack said.
In a later interview on the Fox Business Network, Hammack said she believes the job market is in balance and that the U.S. central bank appears unlikely to achieve its price pressure target even by next year. "My forecast is that inflation is going to end this year around 3% and I think we're not going to make significant progress next year. I think we'll get to maybe mid-twos at best," Hammack said on the network's "Big Money Show" program.
'WATCH THE DATA'

As Jackson Hole conference kicks off, three Fed officials issue inflation warnings

2026-08-28

Por Michael S Derby

https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/jackson-hole-conference-kicks-off-143304791.html

As Jackson Hole conference kicks off, three Fed officials issue inflation warnings

By Michael S. Derby

5 min read

By Michael S. Derby

Aug 27 (Reuters) - Federal Reserve officials shared on Thursday their ongoing concerns about the U.S. inflation landscape, as central bankers gathered in Jackson Hole, Wyoming for the Kansas City Fed's closely watched annual economic symposium.

Inflation is "still stubborn and it's still sticky and we've got to continue to find ways to break through" and get it back to 2%, Kansas City Fed President Jeffrey Schmid said on CNBC on the sidelines of the conference.

He noted that the U.S. central bank's current policy rate, which was left in the 3.50%-3.75% range at the July 28-29 meeting, did not appear to be restrictive. "I don't know what we're restricting currently with the rate policy that we're at today," Schmid said.

Schmid, who had recently been in favor of raising rates to help bring inflation back down to the Fed's 2% target, seemed to suggest that he would still favor such a path, given his belief that monetary policy is not working to counter current price pressures.

But even so, when asked about the outlook for a rate hike at the Fed's September 15-16 policy meeting, he said, "I think we need a little bit more information. What I'm trying to figure out is the demand side of what's driving both growth and inflation."

Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, also speaking on CNBC, was similarly anxious about inflation and reiterated her ongoing willingness to act to bring price pressures back in line.

"I don't want to prejudge anything," Hammack said, "but I believe now is the time to act."

Hammack, one of three Fed officials who dissented at last month's meeting in favor of a rate hike, said inflation has been above target for more than five years and monetary policy is not doing anything at the moment to restrain the economy in order to lower price pressures.

The Cleveland Fed chief said she is hearing more and more from contacts worried about inflation and she fears the longer this trend continues, the greater the risk to the central bank's credibility. Information from local contacts suggests "we're starting to get some of that inflationary mindset" embedding itself in the economy. "I don't think we're there yet, but that's what I want to make sure we avoid," Hammack said.

In a later interview on the Fox Business Network, Hammack said she believes the job market is in balance and that the U.S. central bank appears unlikely to achieve its price pressure target even by next year. "My forecast is that inflation is going to end this year around 3% and I think we're not going to make significant progress next year. I think we'll get to maybe mid-twos at best," Hammack said on the network's "Big Money Show" program.

He said there is a danger the public could shift toward a view that above-target price pressures are not going away.

The Chicago Fed chief, however, noted that the recent three-month inflation trend "doesn't look terrible." Asked about his outlook for interest rates, Goolsbee said the Fed's policy rate could be lowered over time if there was evidence inflation was heading back

item.title: Alphabet Loses $692 Billion in Market Value as AI Questions Rise
item.author: Carmen Reinicke
item.description:
Alphabet Loses $692 Billion in Market Value as AI Questions Rise
2026-08-28
Por Carmen Reinicke
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/alphabet-loses-692-billion-market-123158437.html
(Bloomberg) -- For much of the last year, Alphabet Inc. has been the Big Tech stock to beat as investors bet that it was the most-likely winner from the artificial intelligence boom.
Most Read from Bloomberg
Alphabet shares hit an all-time high on May 13 after soaring more than 150% in the previous 12 months, putting them among the 25 best performers in the S&P 500 Index over that stretch and far outpacing the other Magnificent Seven technology giants. But the momentum has reversed since then due to questions about a brain drain at Google's parent and fears that the company is losing its edge in AI.
The stock is down 15% from its peak, erasing $692 billion in market value and making it the second-biggest point drag on the S&P 500 in that span. At the crux of the selloff is Alphabet's suddenly shaky standing in the AI race, with its heavy spending on building out the infrastructure to develop the technology and the delayed release of its new Gemini AI model weighing on investor sentiment.
And then there's the personnel issue.
A few months ago, Google lost two top employees to Anthropic PBC and OpenAI. Earlier this month, Jeff Dean, who was key to Google's AI strategy, departed to launch a startup and took several high-profile coworkers with him. And Demis Hassabis stepped down as chief executive officer of the Google DeepMind AI research lab, accepting a new role as chairman. Those moves sent Alphabet shares tumbling 4% on Aug. 5, erasing $186 billion in market value in a single session.
"You've had this kind of brain drain," said Angelo Zino, senior vice president and head of technology at CFRA. "It does pose some risk because it's the area of the market everybody is looking at at this point in time, right? It's, you know, can you monetize AI?"
Of course, Alphabet is hardly the only firm challenged by Big Tech's talent race. Last year, Meta Platforms Inc. poached Ruoming Pang from Apple Inc., where he ran the iPhone maker's AI models team, with a $200 million multi-year compensation package and then brought in a couple of his senior deputies.
Around that time, OpenAI Chief Executive Sam Altman complained that Meta was offering his employees signing bonuses of as much as $100 million to join its top AI team. Meanwhile, OpenAI has lured more than 400 Apple employees with rich salaries and hefty stock option offers. And Apple has sued OpenAI for stealing trade secrets.
At Alphabet, however, turnover questions are just the tip of the iceberg. Its more immediate concerns surround delays in developing its most powerful AI model, Gemini 3.5 Pro, which is behind schedule as the company works on improvements, particularly with its coding capabilities, an area where Alphabet is already seen as lagging Anthropic and OpenAI. Two weeks ago, Google released a new Gemini 3.7 Flash model but gave no update on the timetable for Gemini 3.5 Pro.
"If you're an AI winner, you have a leading-edge model and the market gives you a certain multiple premium, which is what was being seen in the stock over the last, let's say nine to 12 months, which has kind of gone away a little on the margins," said Divyaunsh Divatia, analyst at Janus Henderson.
Reasons for Optimism
Alphabet, however, says progress is coming quickly.
"Our AI momentum and shipping velocity are at an all-time high. We're rolling out model updates within weeks of each other, with Gemini 3.7 Flash becoming our fastest-growing model to date and Gemma surpassing one billion downloads," a Google spokesperson said.
The optimism for Alphabet's AI business stems from the success of its tensor processing unit, or TPU, chips and the overwhelming amount of computing power it has amassed. But it's also facing skepticism about its spending after raising $25 billion in an early August bond of
[Transcripcion recortada]

item.title: Earnings spur software and chip rally, offsetting weakness in other areas of the market: AlphaCheck
item.author: Grace O'Donnell
item.description:
Earnings spur software and chip rally, offsetting weakness in other areas of the market: AlphaCheck
2026-08-28
Por Grace O'Donnell
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/earnings-spur-software-and-chip-rally-offsetting-weakness-in-other-areas-of-the-market-alphacheck-135658418.html
Good morning. Stocks advanced on Thursday after Nvidia's (NVDA) bullish outlook sparked a rally in tech stocks, offsetting weakness elsewhere. Nvidia stock gained over 6% in early trading, while semiconductor stocks like Intel (INTC) and SK Hynix (SKHY) also rose.
Earnings movers Salesforce (CRM), Okta (OKTA), and CrowdStrike (CRWD) also surged by double digits on the backs of strong results and outlooks, spurring a rally in software names as well. Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff called for an end to fears of software disruption, saying, "This nonsense of this SaaSpocalypse, I think it's time for it to stop."
Here's a check of the markets in the first few minutes of trading, based on a heat map powered by Yahoo Finance AlphaSpace data.
Tech (XLK) outperformed the rest of the market as the lone S&P 500 sector in the green. Strength in tech helped counterbalance declines in Utilities (XLU), Energy (XLE), and Communications Services (XLC).
Here are some notable stocks that Yahoo Finance readers are viewing this morning: Nvidia, Sandisk (SNDK), INTC, Marvell (MRVL), CrowdStrike, SK Hynix, Dollar Tree (DLTR).

item.title: Iran and Oman announce progress towards 'future administration’ of the Strait of Hormuz. Iran says they are also talking about joint tolls.
item.author: Ben Werschkul
item.description:
Iran and Oman announce progress towards 'future administration’ of the Strait of Hormuz. Iran says they are also talking about joint tolls.
2026-08-28
Por Ben Werschkul
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/iran-and-oman-move-closer-on-future-administration-of-strait-of-hormuz-tolls-are-in-the-mix-143204896.html
Iran and Oman — the two nations that abut the Strait of Hormuz — met this week and announced new progress toward a "permanent navigational corridor and future administration" of the crucial waterway.
Iran went further, claiming the sides have reached a revenue-sharing agreement on future tolls.
The developments could be new flashpoints with President Trump, who made threats in response to the ongoing talks, including a pledge to bomb Oman if that country "gets in the way."
Meanwhile, immediate effects on shipping levels in the strait are unlikely. The latest update from ship tracking service Kpler shows that transits "remain subdued," with just five crossings on Tuesday, all of them through Iran's preferred route.
Strait traffic has been less than a tenth of prewar levels for weeks, while Trump continues to tout the US blockade and his administration promises new economic sanctions to cut off Iran from the world.
In a note to clients, Signum Global Advisors reacted to the joint announcement, suggesting the progress between Iran and Oman could also put pressure on the US and Iran to make a deal by the fall. It could even get the US on board with joint Iran-Oman control of the strait, due to a variety of factors, including that "the US midterms make the Trump administration vulnerable to last-minute Iranian escalation against Gulf energy infrastructure."
Differing accounts of the talks — but clear progress
This week's round of talks between Iran and Oman saw the two sides offer somewhat different accounts, but with both touting progress.
Iran's military went the furthest, according to the Iranian state-run Sepah News agency, claiming that a revenue-sharing agreement has been reached. It was just the latest signal from Iran that it is determined to impose tolls on shippers despite US wishes.
"Agreements have been reached regarding each country's share of the strait's waters as well as Iran and Oman's share of its revenues," Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps spokesperson Hossein Mohebbi reportedly said.
Sayyid Badr bin Hamad Al Busaidi, Oman's foreign minister, offered his own summary of the talks, which didn't mention revenue sharing but cited a push for "practical arrangements to restore safe navigation".
The Omani official also underlined the unfinished nature of the talks.
"I am hopeful we will soon announce a temporary corridor for the Strait of Hormuz and practical arrangements to restore safe navigation," he said.
The joint statement signed off by both nations, replete with cordial photos of the meeting, discussed a phased-in approach with the two nations eventually taking charge of policing the strait on a permanent basis — in direct contradiction to Trump's often-expressed wishes.

Strait traffic has been less than a tenth of prewar levels for weeks, while Trump continues to tout the US blockade and his administration promises new economic sanctions to cut off Iran from the world.
In a note to clients, Signum Global Advisors reacted to the joint announcement, suggesting the progress between Iran and Oman could also put pressure on the US and Iran to make a deal by the fall. It could even get the US on board with joint Iran-Oman control of the strait, due to a variety of factors, including that "the US midterms make the Trump administration vulnerable to last-minute Iranian escalation against Gulf energy infrastructure."
Differing accounts of the talks — but clear progress
This week's round of talks between Iran and Oman saw the two sides offer somewhat different accounts, but with both touting progress.
Iran's military went the furthest, according to the Iranian state-run Sepah News agency, claiming that a revenue-sharing agreement has been reached. It was just the latest signal from Iran that it is determined to impose tolls on shippers despite US wishes.
"Agreements have been reached regarding each country's share of the strait's waters as well as Iran and Oman's share of its revenues," Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps spokesperson Hossein Mohebbi reportedly said.
Sayyid Badr bin Hamad Al Busaidi, Oman's foreign minister, offered his own summary of the talks, which didn't mention revenue sharing but cited a push for "practical arrangements to restore safe navigation".
The Omani official also underlined the unfinished nature of the talks.
"I am hopeful we will soon announce a temporary corridor for the Strait of Hormuz and practical arrangements to restore safe navigation," he said.
The joint statement signed off by both nations, replete with cordial photos of the meeting, discussed a phased-in approach with the two nations eventually taking charge of policing the strait on a permanent basis — in direct contradiction to Trump's often-expressed wishes.

item.title: Droga en carros con doble fondo y avionetas que iban desde Durán a México, así operaba red de Los Lobos en alianza con el cártel Jalisco Nueva Generación
item.author: Jackeline Beltrán
item.description:
Droga en carros con doble fondo y avionetas que iban desde Durán a México, así operaba red de Los Lobos en alianza con el cártel Jalisco Nueva Generación
2026-08-27
Por Jackeline Beltrán
https://www.primicias.ec/seguridad/operativo-factoria-lobos-droga-avionetas-jalisco-nueva-generacion-131093/
Droga en carros con doble fondo y avionetas que iban desde Durán a México, así operaba red de Los Lobos en alianza con el cártel Jalisco Nueva Generación
La Policía de Ecuador dio un golpe a una estructura de Los Lobos que se dedicaba al tráfico de drogas en alianza con el cártel Jalisco Nueva Generación. Hubo allanamientos en Samborondón, Guayaquil y Durán.
La Policía presentó el dinero y las armas incautadas en el operativo Factoría en Guayas, el 26 de agosto de 2026.
- Foto
Policía del Ecuador
Autor:
Actualizada:
Compartir:
Durante el operativo Factoría, ejecutado la madrugada del 26 de agosto de 2026 contra la organización criminal Los Lobos, la Policía localizó tres pistas clandestinas y un centro de acopio de combustible de avionetas que transportan droga desde Ecuador a México y que tenía como destino final Estados Unidos.
El centro de acopio de combustible estaba oculto en un terreno del cantón Durán, en Guayas, uno de los corredores estratégicos del tráfido de droga en Ecuador. Cuando la Policía llegó al lugar, encontró una avioneta en reparación y varios tanques de combustible con capacidad para 1.000 galones.
Alianza con el cártel Jalisco Nueva Generación
El comandante de Policía, Pablo Dávila, explicó cómo operaba esta estructura de Los Lobos en alianza con el cártel Jalisco Nueva Generación, de México: la droga ingresaba en vehículos de doble fondo hacia los diferentes puntos de acopio, ubicados en Vinces de la provincia de Los Ríos.
Desde esa provincia, "la droga era distribuida a las diferentes avionetas que transportaban la droga hacia México y Estados Unidos", detalló Dávila.
En Ecuador, el cártel mexicano Jalisco Nueva Generación tiene alianzas con bandas criminales locales. Los Lobos han sido identificados como su brazo operador, pero también se han detectado vínculos con Los Tiguerones y Chone Killers, según información policial.
Resultados del operativo Factoría
Durante el operativo de esta madrugada en Durán, los uniformados encontraron una tonelada de clorhidrato de cocaína camuflada en cinco carros. La sustancia estaba lista para ser transportada en una de las avionetas, dijo el comandante de la Policía.
"Actuamos a tiempo, tenemos la droga, tenemos los aprehendidos. Es un fuerte golpe para las economías criminales"
Pablo Dávila, comandante de Policía
El operativo Factoría se llevó a cabo también en Samborondón y Guayaquil, en donde se efectuaron 20 allanamientos. Hay 24 aprehendidos, 17 fueron capturados esta madrugada en los allanamientos y los demás ya estaban recluidos en centros de privación de libertad.
Además, las autoridades encontraron cerca de USD 1 millón en efectivo, 20 vehículos, joyas, una avioneta, 35 celulares y 15 armas de fuego, informó la Fiscalía General del Estado.
Operativo paralelo contra Los Choneros
Además del operativo contra Los Lobos, la Policía también realizó una intervención contra otra peligrosa banda criminal del país: Los Choneros. El procedimiento se llevó a cabo en Guayas, Esmeraldas y Manabí.
Ese operativo, denominado Jericó, dejó 19 detenidos. La red delictiva ingresaba marihuana desde la frontera norte y la transportaba hasta Guayaquil, en donde la distribuían los microtraficantes.
Compartir:
